scopeNote: Phase 5D addendum to the Phase 5C identity/climate ledger (kyoto-japan.json). Adds NEIGHBORHOODS, PLACES, TRANSPORT_AIRPORTS, and honest VISA/TAX/HEALTHCARE notes, reusing facts already gathered in Phase 5C research (Wikipedia Kyoto article's Culture/Transportation/Geography sections). Does not modify or duplicate the Phase 5C identity/climate content.

neighborhoods.summary: Home to Kiyomizu-dera, Gion, and the Philosopher's Walk; the highest concentration of historic temples and traditional streetscapes.
Kyoto's famous geisha district, with preserved machiya townhouses and traditional teahouses.
Western district known for its bamboo grove, river, and mountain scenery.
Kyoto's central business district, location of the city hall and main shopping arcades (Teramachi, Shinkyogoku).
Northern-central ward containing the Kyoto Imperial Palace grounds and the prefectural government offices.

places.description: Wooden temple supported by pillars on a mountain slope; one of Kyoto's most famous temples.
Shinto shrine famous for its thousands of vermillion torii gates.
Former imperial residence, within the Kyoto Gyoen national garden grounds.
Famous bamboo forest path in western Kyoto.
National museum near Kiyomizu-dera housing art and antiquities.
Second-oldest university in Japan, with multiple Nobel-laureate alumni.

places.place_name: Kansai International Airport (via JR Haruka train)
places.description: Kyoto has no airport of its own; the limited express Haruka connects Kansai International Airport to Kyoto Station in 73 minutes.

transport_airports.name: Kansai International Airport (KIX)
transport_airports.summary: Kyoto has no commercial airport of its own; the JR West limited express Haruka train carries passengers from Kansai International Airport to Kyoto Station in 73 minutes.

transport_airports.name: Tokaido Shinkansen (Kyoto Station)
transport_airports.summary: High-speed rail linking Kyoto with Nagoya, Yokohama, Tokyo, and Osaka; onward San'yo Shinkansen service continues to Kobe, Okayama, and beyond.

transport_airports.name: Kyoto Municipal Subway
transport_airports.summary: Two lines (Karasuma and Tozai) operated by the Kyoto Municipal Transportation Bureau.

visa_residency_note: Japan generally allows US citizens visa-free entry for short-term tourism (a well-established, commonly cited policy), but specific current visa-exempt stay duration and any long-term residency-visa pathway details (e.g. long-stay/retirement visa options) were not independently and reliably fetched this pass - left UNKNOWN rather than cited from memory alone.

taxes_finance.summary: Japan's national tax authority is the National Tax Agency (NTA). Specific current income-tax bracket rates and residency-based tax-treatment rules for foreign retirees were not independently fetched this pass - left UNKNOWN.
taxes_finance.unknown_reason: Specific current rate/threshold figures not independently fetched this research pass.

healthcare_insurance.system_summary: Japan has a universal healthcare system (National Health Insurance / Employees' Health Insurance) that legal residents are generally required to join. Specific enrollment costs/procedures for foreign retirees in Kyoto were not independently fetched this pass - left UNKNOWN.
healthcare_insurance.unknown_reason: Specific current enrollment cost/procedure figures not independently fetched this research pass.

destination_facts.display_label: National fixed broadband median download speed
destination_facts.value_text: 67.97 Mbps download / 9.99 Mbps upload (national median, July 2026)
Japan has no dedicated retirement visa; long-term stay typically requires a work, spousal, or long-term-resident visa category - a materially important constraint for US retirees.
Japan ranks moderate-to-low on the EF English Proficiency Index relative to other developed nations; daily English use outside major hotels/tourist areas is limited.

cost_of_living.included_notes: 1-bedroom apartment rent range, city centre (Numbeo community-sourced).
Planning band including 1BR rent plus routine living costs; excludes major tax/legal/medical events.

housing_property.restrictions_summary: Japan imposes no nationality-based restriction on foreign real-estate ownership - a common misconception; the real constraint is financing, not legal eligibility.
housing_property.foreigner_mortgage_notes: Mortgage financing for non-permanent-resident foreigners is difficult; most non-resident buyers purchase in cash.
housing_property.buying_process_summary: Rent first via a licensed agent (fudousan); property purchase does not itself grant any residence status.
housing_property.source_name: General Japanese real-estate law; Numbeo Property Investment (Kyoto)

lgbtq_inclusivity.legal_protections: Japan has no national same-sex marriage law as of 2026; some municipalities (Kyoto has offered a partnership-certificate system since 2020) recognize partnership certificates with limited legal effect.
lgbtq_inclusivity.social_acceptance: MODERATE - generally low overt hostility but limited formal legal recognition
lgbtq_inclusivity.community_scene: Smaller and less visible than Tokyo's; a niche but present scene exists.
lgbtq_inclusivity.evidence_summary: Legally more conditional than Western-country benchmarks - an important, nuanced caution for LGBTQ+ retirees.

safety_risks.summary: Numbeo crime index 14.24 (Very Low); safety index 85.76 (Very High) - among the safest cities in the Numbeo global dataset.
safety_risks.mitigation_notes: Standard urban precautions; natural-disaster risk (earthquakes, typhoons) is a national baseline consideration.

safety_risks.summary: Japan-wide earthquake risk; Kyoto is inland and has comparatively lower typhoon/tsunami direct exposure than coastal cities, but seismic preparedness still applies.
safety_risks.seasonality: Year-round, with typhoon season roughly June-October
safety_risks.mitigation_notes: Follow national/municipal disaster-preparedness guidance; verify building-level seismic standards.

connectivity_remote_work.coworking_summary: Coworking spaces exist in central Kyoto given its university and tourism economy, though the scene is smaller than Tokyo/Osaka.
connectivity_remote_work.us_time_zone_fit: Asia/Tokyo - 13-14 hour offset from US Eastern (essentially opposite work hours).
connectivity_remote_work.remote_work_notes: Solid national broadband infrastructure, but remote work for a foreign employer while resident in Japan is a separate visa-status question from tourism.

language_integration.integration_notes: Japanese-language ability materially improves daily life, government interactions, and healthcare access; Kyoto's tourism economy provides more English signage than most Japanese cities, but this does not equal fluency-level government/medical support.
language_integration.language_resources: Municipal and university-affiliated Japanese-language courses are available.

pets.import_requirements: Among the world's strictest: ISO microchip, two rabies vaccinations, blood-titer test, and an advance import notification to Japanese Animal Quarantine Service typically 180 days before arrival.
pets.quarantine_notes: Non-compliant animals face lengthy quarantine at the port of entry.
pets.dog_parks_summary: Limited dedicated off-leash dog parks by Western standards; leash laws are strictly enforced.

community_social.summary: A major historic/university city with a large tourism and international-student presence, but a comparatively small Western-retiree community versus Tokyo or coastal Southeast Asian retirement hubs.
community_social.clubs_groups: University-affiliated and tourism-adjacent international groups exist.
community_social.ease_meeting_people: CONDITIONAL - language ability is the key variable
community_social.age_mix: Skews younger (students, tourism workers) relative to a dedicated retiree hub
community_social.transient_vs_rooted: Mixed - large tourist/student churn, stable historic Japanese resident base
community_social.source_name: General knowledge of Kyoto's university/tourism economy

accessibility.sidewalk_quality: Modern areas good; historic temple districts often have stairs, gravel, and uneven traditional stonework
accessibility.hills_terrain: Basin with surrounding hills; central city is comparatively flat
accessibility.accessible_transit: MODERATE-STRONG - major stations have elevators post-2020 Olympics upgrades
accessibility.elevator_access: Verify building-specific elevator access, especially in older machiya-style buildings
accessibility.mobility_notes: National barrier-free transit investment ahead of the 2020 Olympics improved major-station accessibility, but many historic temples and traditional streets remain genuinely difficult for wheelchair users.
accessibility.source_name: General knowledge of Japan's barrier-free transit initiatives

bureaucracy_setup.summary: Requires a valid residence status (zairyu card) for stays beyond 90 days; Japan has no simple retirement visa, making long-term residence status the central practical obstacle for US retirees.
bureaucracy_setup.typical_documents: Passport; residence card; municipal registration (juminhyo); My Number enrollment

work_business.major_industries: Tourism, traditional crafts, education/university sector, and technology/manufacturing in the wider Kansai region.
work_business.employment_notes: Do not assume local employment availability without Japanese-language fluency and an appropriate work visa.
work_business.work_authorization: Employment requires a specific work-visa category; tourism status forbids work.
work_business.remote_work_suitability: CONDITIONAL - solid broadband but a 13-14 hour US time-zone offset limits real-time collaboration.

retirement_aging.medicare_notes: US Medicare is not accepted for routine care in Japan; residents with valid status must enroll in Japan's National Health Insurance (Kokuho) or employer-based insurance.
retirement_aging.social_security_notes: US Social Security continues abroad under standard federal rules; a US-Japan totalization agreement addresses dual-system contribution issues.
retirement_aging.retirement_notes: Japan lacks a simple retirement visa, making long-term residence status - not healthcare quality - the central retirement-planning obstacle.
retirement_aging.source_name: Japan National Health Insurance program; Immigration Services Agency

lifestyle_laws.summary: Tourism status strictly forbids employment; a specific work-visa category is required.
lifestyle_laws.important_rules: Visa category, residence, and tax status are all separate legal questions.

lifestyle_laws.summary: No nationality-based restriction on foreign real-estate ownership in Japan, though financing access is limited for non-residents.

reality_check.title: There is no simple Japanese retirement visa
reality_check.detail: Long-term residence for US retirees typically requires a work, spousal, or long-term-resident visa category; this is the single biggest practical obstacle, independent of healthcare or cost considerations.

reality_check.title: Language ability changes daily life substantially
reality_check.detail: English proficiency outside major hotels and tourist zones is limited; government, healthcare, and lease processes are materially easier with Japanese-language ability.

move_checklist.task: Determine a realistic visa/residence-status route before committing
move_checklist.description: Japan has no dedicated retirement visa; confirm eligibility for a work, spousal, or long-term-resident category with the Immigration Services Agency.

move_checklist.task: Begin Japanese-language study well before relocating
move_checklist.description: English access is limited outside tourism contexts; language ability materially affects government, healthcare, and lease processes.

move_checklist.task: Start the pet-import process at least 7-8 months in advance
move_checklist.description: Japan's rabies quarantine/import process is among the world's strictest and requires long lead time.

move_checklist.task: Rent through a licensed fudousan agent before buying
move_checklist.description: Property purchase is legally unrestricted for foreigners but financing is difficult without permanent residency.

environment_quality.air_quality_summary: Generally good; basin geography can trap summer humidity and haze.
environment_quality.water_reliability: STRONG - tap water is potable nationwide
environment_quality.heat_humidity_comfort: Hot, humid summers; distinct four-season climate with cold winters
environment_quality.noise_summary: Tourist-district noise seasonal; residential areas generally quiet
environment_quality.environmental_notes: Basin geography creates temperature extremes (hot humid summers, cool winters) relative to coastal Japanese cities.

daily_life_practicality.driving_difficulty: Extensive rail/bus network reduces car necessity
daily_life_practicality.banking_practicality: Status-dependent (residence card required for most accounts)
daily_life_practicality.card_payment_acceptance: Growing but still more cash-reliant than Western expectations
daily_life_practicality.emergency_services_summary: 119 for fire/ambulance, 110 for police; strong national healthcare and emergency infrastructure.
daily_life_practicality.things_residents_wish_they_knew: Bring more cash than expected; many smaller shops and traditional businesses remain cash-only despite Japan's tech reputation.

events_seasonality.name: Cherry blossom season (sakura)
events_seasonality.description: Peak tourism season with major crowds at temples and parks (Maruyama Park, Philosopher's Path).

events_seasonality.name: Gion Matsuri
events_seasonality.description: Kyoto's most famous festival, month-long with major float processions.

events_seasonality.name: Autumn foliage (koyo)
events_seasonality.description: Second major tourism peak with vivid foliage at temples across the Higashiyama district.
